newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slip to flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slip to flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal cash prices slipped to flat to down 1/8 of a point, losing an early rise of as much as 3/8 of a point as individual investors again showed they had little appetite for tax-exempt issues.
"Retail is not buying, that's why the municipal market is underperforming," a trader said, noting that U.S. Treasuries recently have outperformed their brethren.
Still, institutional demand for new issues was fairly strong, as a number of new issues were repriced with lower yields.
For example, a $174 million offering by New York State Urban Development Corp was repriced by Smith Barney, with the yield in 2027 cut to 5.90 percent from 5.925 percent.
The Virginia College Building Authority's revenue bond offering saw its top yield cut to 5.40 percent from 5.43 percent in 2016 through a syndicate headed by Lehman Brothers.

And Massachusetts Health and Educational Facilities Authority's $34.9 million bonds for Lowell General Hospital were repriced, with the yields cut by five basis points in the 1997 through the 1999 maturities in a deal senior managed by PaineWebber Inc.
Florida Ports Financing Commission $222 million debt sale was repriced by Merrill Lynch & Co, with the top yield cut to 5.67 percent from 5.75 percent.

A competitive $131.3 million revenue bond issue sold by the Public Utilities Commission of the City and County of San Francisco was won by JP Morgan Securities with a true interest cost of 5.2555 percent.
But demand in the secondary market remained lackluster, with much of the institutional business getting done on a swap basis, as cash still appeared to be in fairly short supply.

Traders said that the tax-inspired trades typically seen at this time of year might exert less of an influence because the market's strength has dried up the supply of losing bonds that can be sold for tax credits.

While a huge late afternoon sell program caused the Dow Industrials to skid 80 points to around 6443, traders said that any impact on retail investors, who for months have spurned municipals in favor of equities, would not be felt until Wednesday.

The market also was starting to look ahead to the release of the November unemployment data on Friday, which are expected to show that payrolls rose only 179,000, down from the 210,000-gain seen in October. The Reuters consensus survey of economists also showed they look for the unemployment rate to stay at 5.2 percent.
The March municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell seven ticks to 117-21/32, while the benchmark U.S. Treasury futures gained four ticks to 116.
The MOB spread between the two futures contracts stood at 53 ticks.
Actively quoted issues included Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which were bid at 5.58, up two basis points. Their coupon is 5-1/2 percent.
And Chicago Illinois Skyway Toll Bridge Revenues of January 2016, which pay a 5-3/8 coupon, were offered at 5.50 percent, down two basis points.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $1.98 billion in 46 offerings for Wednesday.
Competitive sales total $588 million in 25 issues. The largest issue is a $320 million Los Angeles Harbor deal at 1200 EST.
Negotiated sales total $1.29 billion in 21 offerings. The largest is a $281 million New York State Dormitory Authority issue through Goldman Sachs & Co.
--Joan Gralla, 212-859-1654
